solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copy shortened fencing tool to stop rodent

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece is pushed inside the other like a stopper

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: something shortened has been cut down, so the weapon loses its final letter

parts.note: the epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A fencer improvises with a cut-down blade to block a rat's hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' reads like purpose, but it means plugging: the trimmed sword fills the middle of the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something is to copy it, doing or saying it again in the same way.

clue.text: Blow from vertical beam very incompletely secured

indicators.note: something secured is held fast, here wrapped inside the other piece
in a down entry a vertical word reads upwards, from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a laser is a beam of light

indicators.note: incompletely means not quite whole, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is trimmed

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by a poorly fixed upright girder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vertical beam' looks like a girder, but in a down entry 'vertical' means the beam word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a setback or misfortune, and a blow is used in exactly that sense of a disappointing turn.

clue.text: Security measures permit carrying weapon

indicators.note: a thing carrying another holds it within itself, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a pass is a permit to enter
a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: Airport security checks whether a permit holder is carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Passwords are secret words used to protect access to accounts and buildings, a form of security measure.

clue.text: Astonished by newly made pocket for streetmap

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other
newly made suggests something made afresh, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
an A to Z is a book of street maps

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished by a freshly made pocket designed to hold a street map.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known British book of street maps, so 'streetmap' supplies its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed and astonished are synonyms for being greatly surprised.

clue.text: That Duke in France, taken in by agronomist, drained ancient water channel

indicators.note: something taken in by another is absorbed into it, so it sits inside
in France says the preceding words are translated into French
a drained vessel has had its contents emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: first of the two outer letters
que is French for that
duc is French for duke
last of the two outer letters

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat is captured by a farming scientist who drained an old Roman water channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' empties the agronomist of everything but its outer letters, which then wrap the two French words.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a bridge or channel built to carry water, famously by the Romans.

clue.text: Ford, in fiscal trouble, is blocking defeat rapidly

indicators.note: to block something is to stand in its way, so this group sits in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to quash is to defeat or crush

indicators.note: a word in trouble is in disorder, so its letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A motor company in financial difficulty is holding up a takeover bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the company, but it is its little Ka model, a small hatchback once common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick as a flash is an idiom meaning very fast or immediately, so it matches rapidly as an adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Delete Twitter back-up that's no good in tablets

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the other one

parts.note: first of two E's, each standing for an ecstasy tablet
Twitter was renamed X

indicators.note: back says the word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
NG is the abbreviation for no good
second of the two E's

explanation.surface: Someone wants to delete a useless social media backup stored on their tablet computers.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so 'tablets' is two E's, which hold X, PU and NG.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge something is to erase or remove it completely, the same as deleting it.

clue.text: Band takes off-roader round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so this word encloses the other

parts.note: a ute is a utility vehicle, a pickup
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A music group drives a four-by-four on a tour of Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a musical group, but it is the verb, as in to band together.
explanation.definitionFit: To band together is to join forces, so band as a verb means to unite.

clue.text: Score in race gathering over New Year

indicators.note: over suggests turning something over, so the word is read backwards
gathering means collecting in, so this word wraps around the other

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Somebody scores during a race held over the New Year holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Year' looks like one phrase, but New is turned over inside TT and Year adds a final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a group of twenty, as in threescore years and ten.

clue.text: Landscape by very first academician

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
1st, read as IST

indicators.note: first also picks out the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: first letter of academician

explanation.surface: A landscape painting by the leading member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' does double duty: it gives IST (1st) and also picks the opening A of academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view, especially a long one over a landscape.

clue.text: Show senior royal dismissing knight's reasonable charge

parts.note: a fair is a show or exhibition

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so that letter is removed from the royal title

parts.note: a prince is a senior member of a royal family
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A senior royal sacks a knight at a show, for a reasonable fee.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, where K is already taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair price is one that is reasonable and not inflated, so it is a reasonable charge.

clue.text: Being injured in autumn, female deer's losing ground

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a hind is a female red deer

explanation.surface: A doe hurt during the autumn is losing ground on the rest of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like part of the surface's grammar, but it is the word whose letters are reworked, placed after the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling behind means failing to keep pace with others, which is the idiom losing ground expresses.

clue.text: Battle to reverse wood's poor treatment

indicators.note: to reverse is to run backwards, so the word for battle is read from its end

parts.note: a war is a battle or conflict
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A struggle to turn back the destruction of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British word for softwood planks of fir or pine; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is an idiom for unfair or harsh treatment.

clue.text: Most generous send nuts to feed baby otter

indicators.note: to feed something is to put food into it, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a young otter is called a kit

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The most generous person posts nuts to feed an orphaned baby otter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food being sent, but it is the signal to scramble the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means generous and considerate, so the superlative kindest means most generous.

clue.text: Messed up by American whisky we hear!

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: rye is an American whiskey

explanation.surface: Someone got messed up drinking American whisky, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means gone wrong or off course, which is what messed up describes.

clue.text: Slips girl note and posy every now and then

parts.note: a miss is a girl
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of posy

explanation.surface: A girl occasionally receives a note and a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Missteps are false steps or blunders, so they are slips in both the literal and figurative sense.

clue.text: Talk loudly over two hounds barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of baying dogs drowns out conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dogs' noise, but in British slang barking means crazy, which signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout someone down is to silence them by talking loudly over them.

clue.text: Notice man in front has tools and helmet

indicators.note: in front places that word at the start, before the word for notice

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
an ad is a notice or advertisement
gear is equipment or tools

explanation.surface: A sign tells a man at the front to carry tools and wear a hard hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the notice first, but 'in front' moves the man ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is anything worn on the head, and a helmet is one example.

clue.text: Ignore son playing rough and very loud

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with, set out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A parent ignores a son playing a rough, noisy game.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug off criticism or a problem is to dismiss it as unimportant, which is to ignore it.

clue.text: Mid-west farmer galloped around there endlessly

parts.note: to gallop is to run fast
C is circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: endlessly means with both ends cut off, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cowboy galloped round the ranch without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: C, short for circa, is the standard abbreviation for around, as with approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a cattle ranch, typical of the American Mid-west and West.

clue.text: Kid banks on judge suppressing fine

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down within, so the outer letters enclose the other piece
banks are the edges of a river, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of judge
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A child relies on a judge to avoid a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but here it is the verb meaning to tease; 'fine' is likewise not a penalty but OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease or fool them, and to joke has that same playful sense.

clue.text: Manager who makes embarrassing remarks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a boss or football team manager, in British slang
second meaning, whimsically: one who makes gaffes

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a gaffer is the boss, especially a football manager; the question mark flags the invented sense of a gaffe-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British usage for a boss, while a gaffe is a social blunder, so a gaffer is jokingly a blunderer.

clue.text: Remove incorrect date on chart, no skill required

indicators.note: incorrect means wrong, so the letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: no here means without, so the word for skill is taken away

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut
art is skill, as in the art of conversation
surface padding: it completes the phrase and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: An easy job: correct a wrong date on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' just finishes the surface; the skill word is lifted out of the chart, leaving its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach something is to separate or take it off, so detach means remove.

clue.text: Unavailability of baked beans emptied cafe

indicators.note: baked means cooked, and cooked letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is cleared out, so just the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of cafe

explanation.surface: A cleared-out cafe has run out of baked beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Baked beans on toast is a British cafe staple, which makes 'baked' look like part of the dish rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence is the state of not being present or available, so it means unavailability.

clue.text: Special equipment for shoot

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Specialist kit is needed for a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests a film or photo session, but it is a plant's new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or shoot of a plant.

clue.text: Beer and wine-drinking teenagers initially warned

parts.note: ale is a beer

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the wine word holds the other letter inside

parts.note: red is a red wine

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of teenagers

explanation.surface: Parents are first alerted to teenagers drinking beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to warn them of danger, so alerted is a synonym of warned.

clue.text: Immediately in favour of detailed articles about women's organisation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened words go either side of the organisation
detailed is read as de-tailed, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: for means supporting
two definite articles, each THE
the WI is the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: Immediate support for detailed articles about a women's group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women; 'articles' means two THEs, each losing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith is a formal adverb meaning at once or without delay, so it means immediately.

clue.text: Buffalo never content to be solitary

indicators.note: content means what is held inside, so the answer lies within the words given

parts.note: found inside these words

explanation.surface: A buffalo is never happy on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the adjective meaning happy, but it is the noun: what the words contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone and solitary both describe being on one's own without company.

clue.text: Fantastic art grade needed for fashion business

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters are reworked freely

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A top mark in art is what you need to work in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the clothing and fashion industry.

clue.text: Woman tackling popular right gets black eye

indicators.note: tackling someone means wrapping arms around them, so this word goes round the other

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
in means popular or fashionable
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A woman takes on a popular right-winger and ends up with a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiner is informal slang for a bruised eye, one that shines with colour.
